requirements.requirement: Every sudo command on node1 is recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: Executor configured sudo to log via syslog facility local2 (Defaults syslog=local2 in /etc/sudoers.d/syslog-local2) and routed local2.* to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via rsyslog. Captured log entries (cmd-0db4ef66d38044b9, cmd-d6805cf622b74448) show lines like 'Aug 26 10:39:46 node1 sudo: antrieb : TTY=unknown ; PWD=... ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/whoami', which include a syslog timestamp, the invoking user (antrieb), and the full command. Post-reboot verification (cmd-0002611105664dd5) confirms new commands continue to be logged, showing the configuration is durable.

requirements.requirement: Sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log
requirements.summary: The rsyslog rule for local2.* discards further processing (~) before the message reaches the catch-all *.info rule that writes /var/log/messages (since /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf is included earlier in rsyslog.conf than the messages rule). Direct evidence (cmd-9a09c7f21c404c2e, cmd-0813ef04af474c13) shows grep for COMMAND= in /var/log/messages returns only pre-config-change entries; commands run after the rsyslog restart (whoami, id, cat, tail) do not appear there, both before and after the reboot (cmd-0002611105664dd5). This satisfies the conventional reading of 'general system log' as /var/log/messages; the systemd journal itself may still retain these lines since journald receives them independently of rsyslog filtering, which is a plausible but minor interpretation gap rather than a demonstrated failure.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: cmd-ca44b466335944aa captured the healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id 16724682..., rsyslog active, 14 log entries). cmd-83f2004d05184353 issued a backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' with an immediate acknowledgement. The node was unreachable mid-reboot (cmd-a210fe652b964380) then returned with boot_id 8a973a0c... (cmd-3d6c0908935048ff), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot exactly. cmd-0002611105664dd5 confirms rsyslog active and sudo logging/exclusion from messages both recovered post-restart. This constitutes a full, coherent restart transition.

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented sudo command logging to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp, verified isolation from /var/log/messages both before and after a full node restart, and provided a complete, coherent restart-evidence trail (baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery) matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were introduced.
limitations: The verification of exclusion from the 'general system log' only checked /var/log/messages; the systemd journal (journalctl) may still independently retain sudo log lines since journald receives them before rsyslog filtering, which was not checked. This is a plausible but unconfirmed interpretation gap rather than an observed failure.

Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before_prepare and after_executor lifecycle snapshots, so package-state integrity around the reboot could not be independently cross-checked beyond the failed-services and socket listings.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task requirements: creating the sudoers drop-in (cmd-b269ff47bfeb4ae5), the rsyslog conf (cmd-976e14fd5c77464b), creating/securing the log file and restarting rsyslog (cmd-3edd4b3605fd47fa), running bounded sudo test commands to generate and verify log entries (cmd-0db4ef66d38044b9, cmd-9a09c7f21c404c2e, cmd-0813ef04af474c13, cmd-d6805cf622b74448, cmd-0002611105664dd5), and the reboot (cmd-83f2004d05184353) performed for the mandated node-restart evidence protocol. 'sudo -k' (inside cmd-0813ef04af474c13) only revokes cached sudo credentials, a trivial and expected side effect of testing, not a harmful mutation. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were found; failed-services and listening-socket snapshots are unchanged aside from expected PID churn from the reboot.
